Therefore is justice far from us, and righteousness doesn’t overtake us. We look for light, but see darkness; for brightness, but we walk in obscurity. We grope for the wall like the blind. Yes, we grope as those who have no eyes. We stumble at noon as if it were twilight. Among those who are strong, we are like dead men.

53.why: those who do their work in the dark, and men groping at noonday as in the night

cites.text: I gave my back to those who beat me, and my cheeks to those who plucked off the hair. I didn’t hide my face from shame and spitting.
Now you shall gather yourself in troops, daughter of troops. He has laid siege against us. They will strike the judge of Israel with a rod on the cheek.

64.why: the back given to those who beat and the face not hidden from spitting, and the judge of Israel struck on the cheek

cites.text: Yahweh says to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool for your feet.”

“I saw in the night visions, and behold, there came with the clouds of the sky one like a son of man, and he came even to the ancient of days, and they brought him near before him. Dominion was given him, and glory, and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion, which will not pass away, and his kingdom that which will not be destroyed.

69.why: sit at my right hand, and one like a son of man given dominion and a kingdom

cites.text: I will tell of the decree. Yahweh said to me, “You are my son. Today I have become your father.

For to us a child is born. To us a son is given; and the government will be on his shoulders. His name will be called Wonderful, Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace. Of the increase of his government and of peace there shall be no end, on David’s throne, and on his kingdom, to establish it, and to uphold it with justice and with righteousness from that time on, even forever. The zeal of Yahweh of Armies will perform this.

70.why: you are my Son, and a child born whose name is Mighty God, Everlasting Father

chapters.heading: CHAPTER 23 - A Cross Carried by a Stranger, a Criminal Given Paradise, and a Curtain Torn
chapters.title: A Cross Carried by a Stranger, a Criminal Given Paradise, and a Curtain Torn
keyNotes: The three charges laid before Pilate are all political, and none of them is the charge they actually convicted Him on. A religious council brings a Roman governor a case about sedition and taxes (Luke 23:2).
The tax charge is a flat lie, and Luke has already given us the evidence - three chapters ago He told them to give Caesar what is Caesar's (Luke 23:2, 20:25).
"So you say" is an affirmation that hands the words back. He does not deny the title; He makes Pilate own having said it (Luke 23:3).
Pilate declares Him innocent three times - and executes Him anyway. Luke wants a Roman reader to notice exactly who failed here (Luke 23:4, 14, 22).
The hearing before Herod is only in Luke. Antipas is in the city for the feast - the same man who wanted to see Him back in chapter 9 (Luke 23:7-8, 9:9).
Herod wanted a miracle and got silence. This is the only place in the Gospels where He answers someone with nothing at all (Luke 23:9).
"Herod and Pilate became friends that very day" is Luke's grimmest aside. The early church read Psalm 2 straight onto this scene - the rulers taking counsel together (Luke 23:12).
"I will therefore chastise him and release him" is a flogging offered as a compromise, for a man he has just called innocent. There is no version of that which is justice (Luke 23:16).
Verse 17, about the customary release at the feast, is absent from some manuscripts. The WEB prints it (Luke 23:17).

Barabbas means son of the father, and Luke says twice what he was in for - insurrection and murder. He is guilty of the precise crime they have accused Yahshua of. The innocent takes the place of the guilty, in public, before the cross is even carried (Luke 23:19, 25).
"Their voices prevailed." Luke does not say the case was made. He says the shouting won (Luke 23:23).

Simon of Cyrene is coming in from the country - a pilgrim who walked into the worst morning in history. He is made to carry the cross "after Jesus," which is the exact phrase Luke used for discipleship (Luke 23:26, 9:23).
The only words He speaks on the way are to women, and they are not about Himself. He is still prophesying about the city (Luke 23:28).
"Blessed are the barren" turns that whole culture upside down. In a world where childlessness was grief, He is describing days when it will be mercy (Luke 23:29).
"Fall on us, cover us" is Hosea, spoken over Samaria before it fell (Luke 23:30).
"If they do these things in the green tree, what will be done in the dry?" is a proverb. If this happens to living wood, what happens to dead (Luke 23:31).
The two beside Him are kakourgoi - wrongdoers, criminals. Given Barabbas's charge and the Roman use of crucifixion, insurrectionists is the likely sense, not petty thieves (Luke 23:32).

"Father, forgive them, for they don't know what they are doing" is missing from several early manuscripts and present in many others. The WEB prints it. It is also the exact thing Isaiah 53 said the servant would do - make intercession for the transgressors (Luke 23:34).
The casting of lots is Psalm 22 verbatim, and Luke reports it without a word of commentary. He trusts his reader (Luke 23:34).
Three mockeries, and all three say the same thing: save yourself. The rulers, the soldiers, and one of the criminals (Luke 23:35, 37, 39).
"He saved others" is meant as sarcasm and comes out as testimony. It is true, and it is the reason He will not come down (Luke 23:35).
The inscription is written in three languages, which means the charge was also a proclamation in every language in that street (Luke 23:38).
The second criminal's speech contains a confession, an acquittal, and a request - and he is the only person in the Gospels who asks for the Kingdom and is answered on the spot (Luke 23:40-42).
Think about what he is believing. He is asking a man dying beside him to remember him when He comes into a kingdom. There is no evidence in front of his eyes for any of it (Luke 23:42).
Paradise is the word the Greek Old Testament uses for the garden in Eden. The first man was put out of it; the last words of a dying criminal get him back in (Luke 23:43).
Darkness from the sixth hour to the ninth is noon until three, which is not an eclipse - Passover falls at full moon. Amos said the sun would go down at noon (Luke 23:44).
Luke puts the tearing of the veil before the death; Matthew and Mark put it after. The order differs and the meaning does not - the way in is open (Luke 23:45).
"Father, into your hands I commit my spirit" is Psalm 31, the prayer Jewish mothers taught children to say at bedtime. He adds one word to it: Father (Luke 23:46).
Luke's centurion says "certainly this was a righteous man" where Mark has son of God. Luke has been building a case for innocence all chapter, and he lets a Roman close it (Luke 23:47).
The crowds go home beating their breasts - the same gesture as the tax collector in the temple (Luke 23:48, 18:13).
Joseph of Arimathaea is a council member, and Luke pauses to say he had not consented to their decision. Somebody in that room voted no (Luke 23:50-51).
The tomb had never been used - the same note Luke made about the colt. What is set apart for Him is unused (Luke 23:53, 19:30).
The women see where He is laid, and Luke says so deliberately. He is establishing the chain of witnesses before he needs it (Luke 23:55).
The last thing anybody does before the resurrection is keep the Sabbath according to the commandment. Spices prepared, and then obedience, and then the tomb (Luke 23:56).

intro: Before Pilate the charges change. In front of the council it was blasphemy; in front of a Roman governor blasphemy is not a crime, so three new ones are produced - perverting the nation, forbidding tribute to Caesar, and claiming to be a king. The middle charge is simply a lie, and the evidence sits three chapters earlier, where He told them to give Caesar what is Caesar's, in answer to a question they asked Him.

Pilate examines Him and finds no guilt, then hears the word Galilee and sees a way out, because Galilee is Herod's jurisdiction and Herod is in the city for the feast. That hearing is only in Luke. Herod is delighted - he had wanted to see Him for a long time and is hoping for a miracle. He wants a show, and he is given silence. It is the only place in the four Gospels where a man is answered with nothing at all; Herod had already had his answer once and beheaded the man who brought it.

Then one of the saddest lines in the book: Herod and Pilate became friends that very day, having been enemies before. Nothing unites people like a shared injustice. And back before Pilate the compromise offered is a flogging for a man he has three times pronounced innocent, which is a governor trying to buy off a crowd with somebody else's back.

Barabbas is described twice as a man imprisoned for insurrection and murder - the very charge brought against Yahshua. A guilty insurrectionist walks free and an innocent man is condemned in his place, publicly, before the cross is even lifted. The whole Gospel is acted out in the courtyard before it is accomplished on the hill. And Luke's verdict on how it happened is that their voices prevailed. Not their case; their volume.

Simon of Cyrene is coming in from the country - a pilgrim who arrived for a feast and walked into this - and the cross is laid on him to carry behind Jesus, which is the exact phrase used in chapter 9 for taking up a cross and coming after Him. Then the only words spoken on that road, and they are not about Himself. Daughters of Jerusalem, weep for yourselves. On the way to His own execution He is still grieving over that city.

Father, forgive them is missing from several early manuscripts and printed in the WEB, and it is worth saying plainly that Isaiah 53 had already promised a servant who would make intercession for the transgressors. The mockery comes three times and each time it is the same taunt - save yourself - and the accidental testimony inside it, that He saved others, is exactly why He would not. Then the criminal, who can see nothing but a man bleeding to death under a placard making a joke of His kingship, and who calls it a kingdom and asks to be in it. There is no greater act of faith in the book, and the word he is answered with, Paradise, is the word the Greek Old Testament uses for the garden a man was once put out of. Darkness comes at noon, which cannot be an eclipse at full moon, and the curtain tears - before the death in Luke, after it in Matthew and Mark, with the meaning unchanged: the way in is open, and it was opened from the inside. And He dies saying Psalm 31, the bedtime prayer Jewish children were taught, with one word added to it. Father. The last thing anyone does before the resurrection is keep the Sabbath according to the commandment - obedience, in the dark, with everything lost.

verses.54: It was the day of the Preparation, and the Sabbath was drawing near.
verses.55: The women, who had come with him out of Galilee, followed after, and saw the tomb, and how his body was laid.

chapters.heading: CHAPTER 24 - An Empty Tomb, Seven Miles With a Stranger, and Hands Lifted in Blessing
chapters.title: An Empty Tomb, Seven Miles With a Stranger, and Hands Lifted in Blessing
keyNotes: "On the first day of the week, at early dawn" - the first possible moment after the Sabbath they had just kept. The delay was obedience, not indifference (Luke 24:1, 23:56).
They bring spices for a body, which tells you exactly what they expected to find. Nobody in this chapter is braced for a resurrection (Luke 24:1).
Luke calls them "two men in dazzling clothing" in the narration; it is the women who report them as angels a few verses later (Luke 24:4, 23).
"Why do you seek the living among the dead?" The announcement comes as a question, and the question does the work (Luke 24:5).
"Remember what he told you" - the first resurrection sermon is an appeal to memory. He had said this, more than once, and it had gone straight past them (Luke 24:6-8).

Luke names the women - Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James. Joanna was the wife of Herod's household steward, which is how a movement in Galilee had a source inside the palace (Luke 24:10, 8:3).
In that culture a woman's testimony carried little legal weight. Every Gospel makes women the first witnesses anyway. Nobody inventing a story chooses that (Luke 24:10-11).
"Seemed to them to be nonsense" - leros, a word used medically for the babbling of the delirious. Luke the physician picked it (Luke 24:11).
Verse 12, Peter running to the tomb, is absent from a few manuscripts. The WEB prints it, and it matches what the Emmaus pair report in verse 24 (Luke 24:12, 24).
"The strips of linen lying by themselves" - a robbed grave does not leave the wrappings behind (Luke 24:12).
Sixty stadia is about seven miles - a walk of two to three hours each way. Hold that number; they do it twice in one day (Luke 24:13).
"Their eyes were kept from recognizing him" is passive. Something was done to their sight, and it is undone at a table (Luke 24:16, 31).
Cleopas is named and his companion is not. Traditions have filled the gap; Luke leaves it open, and the empty seat is easy to sit in (Luke 24:18).
"Are you the only stranger in Jerusalem who doesn't know?" is the finest irony in the book. The only one who fully knows is being treated as the only one who does not (Luke 24:18).
"We were hoping that it was he who would redeem Israel" is the saddest sentence in Luke. Were hoping. Past tense (Luke 24:21).

Count what they already have: the prophecy, the empty tomb, the angels' message, and the men who confirmed it. And they are walking away from the city. Information was never the missing piece (Luke 24:21-24).
"Foolish, and slow of heart to believe in all that the prophets have spoken." The rebuke is not for missing the empty tomb. It is for not having read the prophets properly (Luke 24:25).
"Didn't the Christ have to suffer these things?" - dei once more. The suffering was never a detour around the plan (Luke 24:26).

"Beginning from Moses and from all the prophets" is the first sermon on the Hebrew Scriptures ever preached about Him - and Luke does not record one word of the content. The silence hands the work back to us (Luke 24:27).
"He acted like he would go further." He does not force the door. They have to ask (Luke 24:28).
"Stay with us, for it is almost evening." The recognition comes to people who offered hospitality to a stranger (Luke 24:29).

At the table the guest becomes the host: he took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and gave it. Four verbs, and Luke has used them twice before - at the feeding of the five thousand and in the upper room (Luke 24:30, 9:16, 22:19).
Their eyes are opened and He vanishes in the same instant. Recognition does not depend on Him staying visible (Luke 24:31).
"Weren't our hearts burning within us?" They can only name it afterwards. That is usually how it works (Luke 24:32).
Seven miles back, at night, immediately - and they arrive to find the news has already arrived: He has appeared to Simon (Luke 24:33-34).
That appearance to Peter is never narrated by anyone. Luke mentions it in passing, and Paul lists it first among the witnesses. Whatever was said in it, it was between the two of them (Luke 24:34).
"Peace be to you" is the ordinary greeting, shalom, said in the least ordinary circumstances imaginable (Luke 24:36).
They think He is a spirit. The first-century world was perfectly capable of believing in ghosts; that is not what is being claimed here, and He goes out of His way to rule it out (Luke 24:37, 39).
"A spirit doesn't have flesh and bones." The resurrection body is physical - He offers touch, shows the wounds, and then eats in front of them (Luke 24:39-43).
"While they still didn't believe for joy" is the most human line in the chapter. It is possible for something to be too good to take in (Luke 24:41).
"The law of Moses, the prophets, and the psalms" is the threefold Hebrew canon named by its parts. He says the whole of it is about Him (Luke 24:44).
"Then he opened their minds." Three things are opened in this chapter - their eyes, the Scriptures, and their minds - and He does all three (Luke 24:31, 32, 45).
"Repentance and remission of sins preached in his name to all the nations, beginning at Jerusalem" is the table of contents for the book Luke writes next (Luke 24:47).
"Clothed with power from on high" - enduo, to be dressed in something. They are told to wait before they work (Luke 24:49).

He lifts His hands and blesses them, which is the priest's posture in Leviticus. This Gospel opened with a priest who came out of the sanctuary unable to speak the blessing. It closes with a priest whose blessing is not interrupted (Luke 24:50-51, 1:22).
He is still blessing them as He goes. The sentence is never finished, which is the point (Luke 24:51).
The last verse leaves them continually in the temple, praising God - in the building He wept over and said would fall. The Gospel that began there ends there (Luke 24:53, 1:9).

intro: The women come at first light on the first day of the week, which is the earliest moment available to them, because the day before was the Sabbath and they had kept it. And they are carrying spices, which says everything about what they expected. Nobody in this chapter is expecting a resurrection; they came to finish a burial.

The stone is moved, the body is gone, and what the two men in dazzling clothes say is not an announcement but a question. Why do you seek the living among the dead. And then: remember how He told you. The first resurrection sermon ever preached is an appeal to memory. He had said it more than once, and it had gone straight through them.

Luke names the women, including Joanna, whose husband managed Herod's household - which is how this movement had a source inside that court. And the eleven regard the report as an idle tale, using a word a physician would use of the babbling of someone in a fever. It is worth noticing that anyone inventing this story in the first century would not have chosen women as the first witnesses, since their testimony did not count in court. Every Gospel does it anyway.

Then seven miles to Emmaus, and He walks it with two of them while their eyes are kept from recognising Him - kept, passively, something being done. Cleopas asks the funniest question in the New Testament without knowing it: are you the only visitor in Jerusalem who does not know what has happened? The one man who knows everything is treated as the one who knows nothing. And then the saddest sentence in the Gospel, in the past tense: we had hoped that He was the one to redeem Israel.

Consider what they already have. The prophecy, the empty tomb, the report of angels, and men who went and confirmed it - and they are walking out of town. Information was never the missing piece. And the rebuke is not for missing the empty tomb but for not having read the prophets properly. Was it not necessary that the Christ should suffer these things and enter into His glory. Then, beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, He interprets everything concerning Himself - and not one word of it is recorded. Seven miles of the risen Messiah teaching the Hebrew Scriptures about Himself, and no transcript. That silence looks deliberate: the conclusions are not handed over, the road has to be walked.

At the village He acts as though He would go further, because He does not invite Himself in - and it is people who offered hospitality to a stranger who end up recognising Him. At the table the guest becomes the host, taking, blessing, breaking and giving, the same four verbs as the five thousand and the upper room. Their eyes open and He vanishes in the same instant, and only afterwards can they name what was happening on the road. They walk the seven miles back in the dark and arrive to find the news already there: He has appeared to Simon - an appearance nobody ever narrates, because some restorations are private. He shows hands and feet, offers touch, and eats a piece of fish, because this is not a vision or a spirit or a metaphor; and Luke gives us the phrase they still disbelieved for joy, which is a thing too good to get in the door. Then the whole Hebrew Bible named by its three parts and claimed as being about Him, and three things opened in one chapter - eyes at a table, Scriptures on a road, minds in a room. And at the end He lifts His hands in the posture of a priest. This Gospel opened with a priest who went in to burn incense while the people waited outside for the blessing, and who came out unable to speak. It closes with a Priest whose blessing is not interrupted, and the grammar leaves Him blessing them as He goes.

verses.22: Also, certain women of our company amazed us, having arrived early at the tomb;
verses.23: and when they didn’t find his body, they came saying that they had also seen a vision of angels, who said that he was alive.
verses.24: Some of us went to the tomb, and found it just like the women had said, but they didn’t see him.”
verses.25: He said to them, “Foolish men, and slow of heart to believe in all that the prophets have spoken!
verses.26: Didn’t the Christ have to suffer these things and to enter into his glory?”
verses.27: Beginning from Moses and from all the prophets, he explained to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself.
verses.28: They came near to the village, where they were going, and he acted like he would go further.
verses.29: They urged him, saying, “Stay with us, for it is almost evening, and the day is almost over.” He went in to stay with them.
verses.30: When he had sat down at the table with them, he took the bread and gave thanks. Breaking it, he gave it to them.
verses.31: Their eyes were opened, and they recognized him, and he vanished out of their sight.
verses.32: They said to one another, “Weren’t our hearts burning within us, while he spoke to us along the way, and while he opened the Scriptures to us?”
verses.33: They rose up that very hour, returned to Jerusalem, and found the eleven gathered together, and those who were with them,
verses.34: saying, “The Lord is risen indeed, and has appeared to Simon!”
verses.35: They related the things that happened along the way, and how he was recognized by them in the breaking of the bread.
verses.36: As they said these things, Jesus himself stood among them, and said to them, “Peace be to you.”
verses.37: But they were terrified and filled with fear, and supposed that they had seen a spirit.
verses.38: He said to them, “Why are you troubled? Why do doubts arise in your hearts?
verses.39: See my hands and my feet, that it is truly me. Touch me and see, for a spirit doesn’t have flesh and bones, as you see that I have.”
verses.40: When he had said this, he showed them his hands and his feet.
verses.41: While they still didn’t believe for joy, and wondered, he said to them, “Do you have anything here to eat?”
verses.42: They gave him a piece of a broiled fish and some honeycomb.
verses.43: He took them, and ate in front of them.
verses.44: He said to them, “This is what I told you, while I was still with you, that all things which are written in the law of Moses, the prophets, and the psalms, concerning me must be fulfilled.”
verses.45: Then he opened their minds, that they might understand the Scriptures.
verses.46: He said to them, “Thus it is written, and thus it was necessary for the Christ to suffer and to rise from the dead the third day,
verses.47: and that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name to all the nations, beginning at Jerusalem.
verses.48: You are witnesses of these things.
verses.49: Behold, I send out the promise of my Father on you. But wait in the city of Jerusalem until you are clothed with power from on high.”
verses.50: He led them out as far as Bethany, and he lifted up his hands, and blessed them.
verses.51: While he blessed them, he withdrew from them, and was carried up into heaven.
verses.52: They worshiped him, and returned to Jerusalem with great joy,
verses.53: and were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.

cites.text: “Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. You shall labor six days, and do all your work, but the seventh day is a Sabbath to Yahweh your God. You shall not do any work in it, you, nor your son, nor your daughter, your male servant, nor your female servant, nor your livestock, nor your stranger who is within your gates;
“‘Six days shall work be done, but on the seventh day is a Sabbath of solemn rest, a holy convocation; you shall do no kind of work. It is a Sabbath to Yahweh in all your dwellings.

1.why: remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy, and a holy convocation with no work done

cites.text: When they tell you, “Consult with those who have familiar spirits and with the wizards, who chirp and who mutter:” shouldn’t a people consult with their God? Should they consult the dead on behalf of the living?
But as for me, I know that my Redeemer lives. In the end, he will stand upon the earth. After my skin is destroyed, then in my flesh shall I see God,

5.why: should a people consult the dead on behalf of the living, and I know that my Redeemer lives

cites.text: For you will not leave my soul in Sheol, neither will you allow your holy one to see corruption.
Your dead shall live. My dead bodies shall arise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust; for your dew is like the dew of herbs, and the earth will cast out the departed spirits.

6.why: you will not leave my soul in Sheol, and your dead shall live, my dead bodies shall arise

cites.text: After two days he will revive us. On the third day he will raise us up, and we will live before him.
Yahweh prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.

7.why: on the third day he will raise us up, and three days and three nights in the belly of the fish

cites.text: Yet it pleased Yahweh to bruise him. He has caused him to suffer. When you make his soul an offering for sin, he will see his offspring. He will prolong his days, and Yahweh’s pleasure will prosper in his hand. After the suffering of his soul, he will see the light and be satisfied. My righteous servant will justify many by the knowledge of himself; and he will bear their iniquities.

Dominion was given him, and glory, and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion, which will not pass away, and his kingdom that which will not be destroyed.

26.why: he shall see his offspring and be satisfied, and dominion given him that will not pass away

cites.text: Yahweh your God will raise up to you a prophet from among you, of your brothers, like me. You shall listen to him.
After the suffering of his soul, he will see the light and be satisfied. My righteous servant will justify many by the knowledge of himself; and he will bear their iniquities.

27.why: a prophet like Moses whom you shall hear, and the righteous servant justifying many

cites.text: Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine: and he was priest of God Most High.
Oh taste and see that Yahweh is good. Blessed is the man who takes refuge in him.

30.why: Melchizedek bringing out bread and wine, and taste and see that Yahweh is good

cites.text: If I say, I will not make mention of him, or speak any more in his name, then there is in my heart as it were a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I am weary with holding it in, and I can’t.
My heart was hot within me. While I meditated, the fire burned. I spoke with my tongue:

32.why: his word like a burning fire shut up in my bones, and my heart was hot within me

cites.text: After my skin is destroyed, then in my flesh shall I see God,
Therefore my heart is glad, and my tongue rejoices. My body shall also dwell in safety. For you will not leave my soul in Sheol, neither will you allow your holy one to see corruption.

39.why: in my flesh I will see God, and my flesh also dwelling in safety

cites.text: Then I said, “Behold, I have come. It is written about me in the book in the scroll.

“Seventy weeks are decreed on your people and on your holy city, to finish disobedience, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most holy.

44.why: in the scroll of the book it is written of me, and everything decreed to finish transgression

cites.text: Indeed, he says, “It is too light a thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel? I will also give you as a light to the nations, that you may be my salvation to the end of the earth.”

It shall happen in the latter days, that the mountain of Yahweh’s house shall be established on the top of the mountains, and shall be raised above the hills; and all nations shall flow to it. Many peoples shall go and say, “Come, let’s go up to the mountain of Yahweh, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths.” For out of Zion the law shall go out, and Yahweh’s word from Jerusalem.

47.why: a light to the nations that salvation may reach the end of the earth, and the word going out from Jerusalem

cites.text: “It will happen afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams. Your young men will see visions. And also on the servants and on the handmaids in those days, I will pour out my Spirit.
Until the Spirit is poured on us from on high, and the wilderness becomes a fruitful field, and the fruitful field is considered a forest.

49.why: I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh, and until the Spirit is poured on us from on high

cites.text: You have ascended on high. You have led away captives. You have received gifts among men, yes, among the rebellious also, that Yah God might dwell there.
As they continued on and talked, behold, a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated them, and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.

51.why: you have ascended on high and led captivity captive, and Elijah going up by a whirlwind into heaven

parts.title: Major Themes Across Luke 1-3
items: A Gospel that opens by explaining its own method, and stakes everything on certainty
An author who was not an eyewitness and says so, working from those who were
The last two verses of Malachi picked up as the first promise of the New Testament
Two questions that look identical - one silenced, one answered - and the difference between them
Gabriel, last seen giving Daniel a timetable, returning to say the time is up
A promise made to David a thousand years earlier, handed to a girl in Nazareth
Presence language - the cloud that overshadowed the tabernacle - used of a womb
A song about thrones being emptied, sung by someone with nothing, entirely in the past tense
Speech returned to a man on the far side of obedience
Saviour, good news and peace on earth - Caesar's words, moved to a feeding trough
Shepherds told first, and a sign that is deliberately unimpressive
Two birds on the altar, and a family whose poverty Luke reports without commenting on
An old man asking to be discharged because the waiting is finally over
A light for the nations announced from inside the temple courts
A sword promised to the mother in the middle of the happiest scene in the book
Eighteen years of obedience compressed into four words
Six rulers named, so that the date can be checked
The prophetic formula returning after four centuries, and landing on nobody important
Isaiah 40 quoted one line further than the other Gospels quote it, and why that line matters
Repentance that changes the ledger and the cupboard rather than the job title
Fire explained by the very next verse, and a fork that decides which baptism you receive
A Messiah who is praying when heaven opens
King and Suffering Servant spoken in one sentence, before He has done anything
A genealogy that runs backwards past Abraham to Adam, and one word further

parts.title: Major Themes Across Luke 4-6
items: A wilderness entered on purpose, led by the Spirit rather than ambushed by the devil
Israel's forty years compressed into forty days, and answered entirely out of Deuteronomy
A devil who leaves until an opportune time, and a Gospel that remembers he said so
A scroll closed mid-sentence, with the day of vengeance left unread
Jubilee announced - debts cancelled, captives released - as the shape of the ministry
The shortest sermon in the Gospels, and the fastest congregation ever to turn
A Sidonian widow and a Syrian commander, chosen for maximum offence
Rejection at home placed at the start of the ministry rather than the middle
A physician's eye: a great fever, no harm done, hands laid on every single one
The word must, which in this Gospel never means He felt like it
A pulpit borrowed before a disciple is called
Obedience that names the objection honestly and then acts anyway
Abundance that produces confession rather than celebration
A hand that touches a leper, and uncleanness running the wrong way
Withdrawal to pray as a habit, not an occasion
Faith credited to the friends carrying the stretcher
Correct theology used to reach the wrong verdict
New wine that cannot be poured into what has already stretched as far as it goes
A quiet last word about why we prefer the old
A question about saving or killing, answered by a plan to kill
A whole night of prayer before twelve names, including a Zealot and a tax collector
Four blessings and four woes, and poverty that Luke refuses to make a metaphor
Woe for being spoken well of, and what that costs anyone with an audience
Mercy named as the family resemblance where Matthew names perfection
A foundation dug deep, underground, where nobody watching can verify it

parts.title: Major Themes Across Luke 7-9
items: A Gentile officer's faith praised above anything found in Israel, from a man who never appears
Two verdicts on the same man - he is worthy, and I am not worthy
Compassion aimed at the mother rather than the corpse
A hand laid on a bier, and uncleanness running the wrong direction again
Elijah and Elisha's territory, entered a couple of miles from where they worked
The greatest prophet born of women asking, from a cell, whether he was wrong
An answer that gives everything Isaiah promised except the one thing the asker needed
Do you see this woman - asked of a man who had been looking at her all evening
Love as the result of forgiveness rather than its price
A ministry funded by named women out of their own money
Seed, moisture, temptation, and pleasures - Luke's own additions to the sower
Fruit measured by endurance rather than by harvest
A man at His feet, clothed and in his right mind, told to stay rather than follow
A whole region asking Him to leave, and a Messiah who goes
Twelve years of dying and twelve years of bleeding, folded into one interruption
A delay caused by one woman that turned a healing into a resurrection
A mission designed so the sent cannot be self-sufficient
An impossible order given before any means of obeying it exists
Prayer as the setting for the great confession and for the transfiguration
A cross taken up daily rather than once
An exodus discussed on a mountain, with Moses standing there
A voice that adds two words to what it said at the Jordan: listen to him
Incomprehension described as something concealed rather than merely missed
Fire requested by men who had just watched Elijah talk about a rescue
A face set toward Jerusalem, and ten chapters of road that never bends

parts.title: Major Themes Across Luke 10-12
items: Seventy sent ahead into every town He was about to enter, as an advance party
Men told to pray for labourers, and then sent as the answer to that prayer
A joy in successful ministry, gently corrected by a better one
The only place in the Gospels where He is said to rejoice
A lawyer who answers his own question correctly and then looks for a boundary
Two religious professionals going away from the temple, with duty already behind them
A heretic who keeps the law the lawyer had just quoted
Neighbour turned from a category into a verb
A woman in the seat of a student, and a sister pulled in too many directions
A request to be taught prayer, prompted by watching prayer
Shamelessness rather than persistence at a midnight door
An answer to prayer that is finally a Person and not a thing
The finger of God, borrowed from magicians who ran out of tricks
A house swept, ordered, empty - and worse off for it
Herbs tithed and justice skipped, and a rebuke that does not cancel the tithe
Unmarked graves that defile the people walking over them
Yeast, because hypocrisy is never a decision
The one fear that is commanded, aimed away from the people who can kill you
Five sparrows, and the free one God has not forgotten
A man who did not cheat anyone, and said I eleven times
A life called in like a loan on the night the barns were approved
The unclean bird God feeds, offered as the argument against anxiety
Little flock - said once in Scripture, to people with nothing
A master who comes home, puts on an apron, and serves the staff

parts.title: Major Themes Across Luke 13-15
items: A refusal to read guilt off the size of somebody else's disaster
The same warning given twice, to those who brought the news rather than those in it
A barren tree costing the soil more than its silence suggests
A gardener who does not dispute the verdict and asks for one more year
Grace with a spade in its hand, and a reprieve with a date on it
A woman who did not ask, and was called
Loosing, on the day the whole week bends toward
The Sabbath argued from the inside rather than set aside
A daughter of Abraham named out loud in a room that had stopped seeing her
The Kingdom as a garden seed and hidden yeast: small, quiet, and unstoppable
A speculative question about numbers answered with a personal imperative
A door that is open now, and a master who eventually stands up
Proximity mistaken for relationship - we ate and drank in your presence
The only insult He ever gave a ruler, and the timetable no ruler could move
A hen instead of an eagle, and grief before judgment
A desolate house with an until attached to it
A dinner where the guest is under surveillance and heals anyway
Seats as a scoreboard, and a Host who does His own seating
Hospitality unplugged from repayment, with accounts left open until the resurrection
Respectable excuses, deployed against an invitation already accepted
Anger that widens the party instead of cancelling it, and a servant reporting there is still room
A crowd that grows, and a Teacher who starts subtracting
Counting the cost, where the counting sometimes ends in terms of peace
Salt that is not weak but contaminated, fit for neither soil nor manure pile
One complaint - he eats with sinners - answered three times
Searching that has no stated limit, and carrying that asks nothing of the carried
God imaged as a shepherd and a woman with a lamp, in the same breath
A father who does the shameful running so his son does not have to walk it alone
A confession interrupted before it can become a repayment plan
Robe, ring and shoes given instead of a job
A son who lived as an employee in a house where he was always an heir
This your son, and this your brother, and a story that stops so the hearer must finish it

parts.title: Major Themes Across Luke 16-18
items: A crooked man commended for the one thing he got right - he saw what was coming
The children of this age out-thinking the children of light about their own future
Money as somebody else's property, passing through your hands as a test
Mammon promoted from a possession to a rival master
Respectability that men exalt and God calls abomination
The Kingdom announced and not one hook of the law allowed to fall
A beggar with a name and a rich man without one
A gate walked past daily by a man who knew the name of the one lying at it
Moses and the prophets treated as warning enough, even against a resurrection
Traps that are certain to come, and a woe reserved for whoever sets them
Rebuke commanded, and forgiveness with no test for sincerity attached
A request for more faith answered with a mustard seed
Obedience that never puts God in our debt
Ten men healed on the road, in the obedience, before any evidence
One who came back, and Luke saving until last that he was a Samaritan
Ten cleansed and one made whole
A Kingdom that will not be found by the kind of watching that looks for signs
The cross set down in the middle of the end of the world
Judgment falling on eating, drinking, buying, building - a normality that stopped listening
A woman who did not turn back, only looked
A widow whose only weapon was that she would not go away
A delay that is patience, and a vindication called speedy
The real question - not whether He will answer, but whether faith will still be asking
A prayer with no request in it, and every claim in it true
A man who asked for atonement, not for leniency, and called himself the sinner
A verdict of justified handed to the one who could not lift his eyes
A child who can only receive, set next to a ruler who wants the price
One commandment left off the list, and it was the one that mattered
Sell, distribute, come, follow - three instructions serving the fourth
A camel and a needle, meant to be impossible, and an answer that is only ever God
A saying hidden from the twelve even as He explained it
A blind beggar shouting a title nobody else in this Gospel had shouted yet
Three people with no standing at all, and all three of them heard

parts.title: Major Themes Across Luke 19-21
items: A rich man who ran and climbed, and got what the rich ruler walked away from
A vow made standing up, harsher than the law required and asked for by no one
Salvation announced over a house the whole town had written off
A Gospel's thesis landing on a tax collector - the Son of Man came to seek and to save
A parable told to slow down people who thought the Kingdom was arriving that week
Everybody given the same mina, and nobody given the same result
Money perfectly preserved and completely wasted
A servant frozen by what he believed about his master
A colt never ridden, for a use that was never ordinary
Cloaks in the road, a psalm with one word added, and a title worth dying for
Peace on earth at the manger, peace in heaven on the donkey
Stones that would take up the shout if the disciples stopped
A King who wailed out loud over the city named for peace
A visitation missed, and forty years of consequences described in advance
A den as the place robbers go to feel safe
An honest question answered with an honest question, twice
Men who calculated the consequences of every answer except the true one
Isaiah's vineyard song with its ending rewritten
An owner whose patience is stranger than the tenants' violence
The heir thrown out first and killed second, exactly as it happened
A coin produced in the temple by the men asking about lawfulness
Caesar's image on the silver, God's image on the man holding it
The resurrection proved from a burning bush, in the only court the Sadducees allowed
A God who says I am, of men centuries in the ground
A question about David's son left hanging in the air, unanswered on purpose
Robes, greetings, best seats - a whole list about being seen
Widows' houses devoured in one verse and a widow's last coins given in the next
Beautiful stones admired and sentenced in the same conversation
Persecution placed first in the sequence, and the dock turned into a pulpit
Some of you put to death, and not a hair of your head lost
A trampling with an until attached to it
Everyone else fainting, and one instruction: look up, lift up your heads
A fig tree and all the trees, because this is about reading a season
A trap that springs on the heavy-hearted, not on the persecuted
A discourse about the end of the world that finishes in prayer

parts.title: Major Themes Across Luke 22-24
items: An opportune time that had been waiting since the wilderness
A betrayer who was counted among the twelve, and never called anything else
A room arranged in advance, and an address the betrayer could not give away
With desire I have desired - a meal He wanted
A cup left undrunk until the Kingdom comes
A memorial rite entered from the inside, and a covenant ratified in blood
An argument about greatness with the bread still in their hands
Kings called benefactors, and a Lord who called Himself a servant
A sifting aimed at all of them and a prayer prayed for one
A faith kept from failing rather than a man kept from falling
Work assigned on the far side of a failure that had not happened yet
Two swords, and the only wound they caused healed within the hour
A cup asked about honestly and then accepted completely
An hour with a name, an owner, and an end
A look across a courtyard that was not the end of Peter
Charges that changed to fit the court
Three verdicts of innocent and an execution anyway
Two enemies made friends over a shared injustice
A guilty man released and an innocent man taken in his place
A pilgrim from Cyrene carrying a cross behind Him
Words on the road spent on somebody else's children
Save yourself, said three times to the one person who would not
A criminal who saw a kingdom where everyone else saw an execution
Paradise given away by a dying man with nothing to give
Darkness at noon, and a curtain torn from the inside
A childhood bedtime prayer with one word added: Father
A council member who voted no, recorded even though it changed nothing
A grave nobody had used, like a colt nobody had ridden
Obedience to the Sabbath as the last act before the resurrection
Spices carried by people who expected a body
An announcement that arrived as a question
Women believed by nobody and recorded by everybody
A hope in the past tense, walking away from the city
Seven miles of the Scriptures explained, and not one line written down
A guest who becomes the host, and four verbs that give Him away
Eyes, Scriptures and minds - three things opened, all by Him
Disbelieving for joy
Flesh and bones, and a piece of fish eaten to prove it
A blessing interrupted in chapter one and never interrupted again
A Gospel that ends in the temple, in joy, waiting to be clothed
